abhasa.gloss: appearance, glow: every thing is the light of Consciousness that has taken the form of that thing, not something alongside it.
abhasa.name: Ābhāsa

abheda.gloss: non-distinction, unity — the view in which there is no separateness.
abheda.name: Abheda

aham.gloss: "I" — not the human "I," but the full I of God, containing the universe.
aham.name: Aham

ahanta.gloss: "I-ness": that something is taken as "I." The counterpart to idantā.
ahanta.name: Ahantā

akula.gloss: “outside the family”: Śiva, taken as that from which Kula proceeds and which itself is contained in nothing.
akula.name: Akula

amrta.gloss: the nectar of immortality: the same Bliss, taken as that by which Consciousness nourishes itself.
amrta.name: Amṛta

ananda.gloss: Bliss — not an experience among others, but the very nature of Consciousness: fullness that needs nothing.
ananda.name: Ānanda

anava.gloss: pertaining to the individual being (aṇu): as a path — with support on the body, breath, object; as a mala — the original “I am incomplete.”
anava.name: Āṇava

anugraha.gloss: Grace — the fifth act of God: that by which He reveals Himself.
anugraha.name: Anugraha

anupravesha.gloss: entering — the same immersion, taken as a transition inward.
anupravesha.name: Anupraveśa

anuttara.gloss: “that above which there is nothing”: the Supreme Reality, from which everything proceeds and in which everything rests. In this treatise, also the name of the sound “a,” with which the alphabet and the mantra itself begin.
anuttara.name: Anuttara

apara.gloss: “nonsupreme” — the third of the three Goddesses: the side of complete differentiation, where things stand apart.
apara.name: Aparā

artha.gloss: meaning and object — that which is denoted. In the phrase “that is” in Gabriel, arthaḥ simply means “the meaning is such.”
artha.name: Artha

bhagavati.gloss: “Blessed One,” “Mistress” — the Goddess; in the masculine, bhagavat, “Blessed Lord.”
bhagavati.name: Bhagavatī

bhairava.gloss: the name of the Supreme Lord in Trika: He who holds the universe, bears it, and draws it back into Himself. Not a “terrifying deity,” but the fullness of Consciousness.
bhairava.name: Bhairava

bhattaraka.gloss: “venerable Lord” — a respectful address to Śiva or Bhairava.
bhattaraka.name: Bhaṭṭāraka

bhattarika.gloss: “venerable Mistress” — the same, of the Goddess, most often of Parā.
bhattarika.name: Bhaṭṭārikā

bheda.gloss: difference, separateness — the view in which things stand apart.
bheda.name: Bheda

bija.gloss: “seed”: a vowel sound — that from which a syllable grows; hence also a short mantra of one syllable.
bija.name: Bīja

bindu.gloss: point: the indivisible drop of Light in which everything is contained; in writing, the sign “ṁ.”
bindu.name: Bindu

bodha.gloss: awakeness, knowledge as such; in translation often simply "Consciousness."
bodha.name: Bodha

camatkara.gloss: wonder-delight: the taste with which Consciousness knows itself, an "ah!" without external cause.
camatkara.name: Camatkāra

cit.gloss: Consciousness as the pure Light of knowledge; citi — the same as an active power.
cit.name: Cit

hrdaya.gloss: Heart — not an organ, but the center: the Supreme Self itself, in which everything converges.
hrdaya.name: Hṛdaya

iccha.gloss: Will — the force with which every action of God begins.
iccha.name: Icchā

idanta.gloss: "this-ness": that something is taken as "this," as an object opposite.
idanta.name: Idantā

ishvara.gloss: the fourth stage: “This is I” — the universe is clearly manifested and rests on the Self.
ishvara.name: Īśvara

jivanmukta.gloss: liberated while living: one who is free without leaving the body.
jivanmukta.name: Jīvanmukta

jnana.gloss: Knowledge — the second of the three forces; jñāna-śakti — it is also directly called the Force.
jnana.name: Jñāna

kala.gloss: a particle, a portion of the Force: both Absolute Freedom as a “particle” of the Highest, and a stage of manifestation that limits activity. Not to be confused with kāla — time.
kala.name: Kalā

kaulika.gloss: pertaining to Kula; kaulikī siddhi — “Kaulic perfection,” that power by which the Goddess manifests the universe.
kaulika.name: Kaulika

khecari.gloss: “moving in space”: a state in which consciousness moves in the open expanse of Consciousness itself.
khecari.name: Khecarī

kriya.gloss: Action — the third force: that by which Will and Knowledge become deed.
kriya.name: Kriyā

ksobha.gloss: perturbation: the movement by which the repose of Consciousness turns into manifestation.
ksobha.name: Kṣobha

kula.gloss: “family, host”: the Body of Consciousness — everything the Supreme contains within itself. Hence also the name of the Kaula tradition.
kula.name: Kula

madhyama.gloss: “the middle one” — the third level: inner speech, with words, but not uttered.
madhyama.name: Madhyamā

mahamantra.gloss: “the great mantra” — here sauḥ, the mantra of the Goddess Parā, about which the entire treatise is written.
mahamantra.name: Mahā-mantra

mala.gloss: “impurity”: not dirt, but constraint by which Consciousness limits itself. There are three: āṇava — “I am incomplete,” māyīya — “the world is alien to me,” kārma — “I am the doer.”
mala.name: Mala

malini.gloss: the same alphabet, but in a mixed order, where vowels and consonants are interwoven.
malini.name: Mālinī

mantra.gloss: not an incantation, but sound together with I-Consciousness: it acts not by meaning, but by power (vīrya).
mantra.name: Mantra

matrka.gloss: “Mother”: the alphabet as a host of powers, from which both all speech and all worlds are born.
matrka.name: Mātṛkā

maya.gloss: the Power by which God makes Himself many and hides Himself from Himself. In Trika this is not deception, but real division.
maya.name: Māyā

nara.gloss: man, the bound being — the third in the triad Śiva — Śakti — Nara.
nara.name: Nara

nirvikalpa.gloss: thought-free knowledge: the same Consciousness before a boundary is laid in it. The same — avikalpa.
nirvikalpa.name: Nirvikalpa

pada.gloss: word; also a state, a stage, a “place” on which one stands.
pada.name: Pada

para.gloss: “Supreme”: the Goddess Parā — and the highest, not yet divided level of Speech. In compounds, para simply means “supreme.”
para.name: Parā

paraapara.gloss: “supreme-nonsupreme” — the second of the three Goddesses: unity within which distinction is already visible.
paraapara.name: Parā-aparā

paramaishvara.gloss: “Supreme Lord” — God taken as the master of manifestation; in the feminine, pārama-īśvarī, His Mistress.
paramaishvara.name: Parameśvara

paramarsha.gloss: grasping, awareness: the same response taken as a separate flash — consciousness takes something as "this" or as "I."
paramarsha.name: Parāmarśa

pashyanti.gloss: “the seeing one” — the second level of Speech: meaning is already present, but not yet divided into words.
pashyanti.name: Paśyantī

prakasha.gloss: Light: that by which everything is manifested. Alone, without a response to itself, it would be a light that does not know it shines.
prakasha.name: Prakāśa

pramatr.gloss: the knower, the subject. Together with pramāṇa (knowledge itself, the measure) and prameya (the knowable) it forms the triad on which all perception rests.
pramatr.name: Pramātṛ

prana.gloss: the vital breath by which the body is held; here also the level on which unspoken speech sounds.
prana.name: Prāṇa

prasara.gloss: spreading: the exit of Power outward.
prasara.name: Prasara

pratibha.gloss: flash of insight: the light in which meaning opens at once and in its entirety.
pratibha.name: Pratibhā

sadashiva.gloss: the third stage: “I am this” — the universe is already seen, but vaguely and within the Self.
sadashiva.name: Sadāśiva

samavesha.gloss: immersion, in which the being coincides with Śiva.
samavesha.name: Samāveśa

samhara.gloss: drawing the manifested back — not destruction, but return into Consciousness.
samhara.name: Saṁhāra

samvid.gloss: Consciousness — not a property of a person, but the sole Reality that knows itself. The same as cit; saṁvitti — the same as a state.
samvid.name: Saṁvid

sanketa.gloss: convention: the conditional correspondence of word and object, on which ordinary speech rests.
sanketa.name: Saṅketa

sankoca.gloss: contraction: the same Consciousness, drawn tight to a separate being. Its opposite is vikāsa, expansion.
sankoca.name: Saṅkoca

shabda.gloss: sound, word — that by which one denotes; the counterpart of artha.
shabda.name: Śabda

shakta.gloss: pertaining to Śakti; as a path — the path of Knowledge and awareness.
shakta.name: Śākta

shakti.gloss: God’s Power, His Self-awareness: the same Reality taken as will and movement. Śiva without Śakti manifests nothing, and there is no difference between them.
shakti.name: Śakti

shaktipata.gloss: “descent of Power”: the moment in which Grace touches a person.
shaktipata.name: Śaktipāta

shambhava.gloss: the path of Śambhu — the highest: without support, by Will alone.
shambhava.name: Śāmbhava

shastra.gloss: treatise, body of rules; śāstreṣu — “in the scriptures.”
shastra.name: Śāstra

shiva.gloss: God as the resting side of Reality — the Light of Consciousness, not different from His own Power.
shiva.name: Śiva

shivatattva.gloss: the first of the thirty-six stages: the Light in which nothing is yet distinguished.
shivatattva.name: Śiva-tattva

shuddhavidya.gloss: the fifth stage, “pure knowledge”: Self and this stand on equal footing.
shuddhavidya.name: Śuddhavidyā

siddhi.gloss: attainment, perfection — and the superordinary power that accompanies it.
siddhi.name: Siddhi

spanda.gloss: quiver: a slight movement within the motionless, by which all manifestation is held.
spanda.name: Spanda

sphurana.gloss: flaring, flickering — how Consciousness manifests itself; sphurattā — the same as a state.
sphurana.name: Sphuraṇa

srsti.gloss: manifestation, “emission” of the world — the first of God’s five actions.
srsti.name: Sṛṣṭi

sthiti.gloss: maintenance of the manifested, its standing — the second action.
sthiti.name: Sthiti

svatantrya.gloss: absolute Freedom: God’s capacity to be anything and manifest anything, without being bound by anything.
svatantrya.name: Svātantrya

tadatmya.gloss: identity, “same-naturedness”: not the similarity of two things, but the coincidence of their essence.
tadatmya.name: Tādātmya

tattva.gloss: “suchness”: a stage of manifestation. There are thirty-six of them — from Śiva to earth.
tattva.name: Tattva

trika.gloss: “the triple” — this very system: it analyzes the triad Śiva — Śakti — Nara, and it is also the triad of Goddesses Parā, Parā-aparā, Aparā.
trika.name: Trika

turya.gloss: “fourth” state — beyond waking, dreaming sleep, and deep sleep.
turya.name: Turya

unmesa.gloss: "opening of the eye": the moment in which Consciousness opens wide and the universe appears.
unmesa.name: Unmeṣa

upadesha.gloss: instruction: the oral indication of the teacher, not knowledge read from books.
upadesha.name: Upadeśa

upaya.gloss: means, path. There are three — śāmbhava, śākta, āṇava: according to what one proceeds by — Will, Knowledge, or effort.
upaya.name: Upāya

vacaka.gloss: the signifier — the word; the signified, the object, is called vācya.
vacaka.name: Vācaka

vaikhari.gloss: “the bodily one” — the fourth level: speech uttered aloud.
vaikhari.name: Vaikharī

vak.gloss: Speech — not language, but the very power of utterance. It passes through four levels: parā, paśyantī, madhyamā, vaikharī.
vak.name: Vāk

varna.gloss: letter-sound: not a written sign, but the sound itself, taken as a power.
varna.name: Varṇa

vidya.gloss: Knowledge — both as the Force of God and as the limited knowledge of the bound being.
vidya.name: Vidyā

vikalpa.gloss: thought, a distinguishing representation: "this, not that." By it the one is cut into pieces.
vikalpa.name: Vikalpa

vimarsha.gloss: the response of Light to itself, I-Consciousness: "I am." Prakāśa and vimarśa are two sides of one thing, not two things.
vimarsha.name: Vimarśa

virya.gloss: power. mantra-vīrya — the Power of the mantra: that very Self-Consciousness without which the mantra remains sound.
virya.name: Vīrya

visarga.gloss: Emission: that by which the Highest pours itself into the world. In writing — the sign “ḥ,” two dots, and in the treatise they are read as its two faces.
visarga.name: Visarga

vishranti.gloss: rest, repose: a stopping in oneself, to which everything ultimately reduces.
vishranti.name: Viśrānti

yamala.gloss: “pair”: the indivisible couple of Śiva and Śakti — and that state which is born of their union.
yamala.name: Yāmala

yoni.gloss: “womb”: a consonant sound — that in which the seed unfolds; and the Goddess herself as the source.
yoni.name: Yoni
